note: Sky's OK 2026-10-27 covers this budget only; at most one retry per mesh, for a clear failure

model.note: Runware's page (https://runware.ai/docs/models/tencent-hunyuan-3d-3-1-pro): image-to-3d $0.525 textured, $0.825 with PBR; the game's figures are matte, so no PBR. The estimate is held at the PBR price, so the budget stop is conservative if multi-view costs more. faceCount 50000 as today's D-cast (PROVENANCE.json).

hat.note: the hybrid's hat, cut by whole shells: image-to-3D meshes are hundreds of separate shells, and a hat is usually its own shells sitting on the hair. A shell is the hat's when at least shellShare of its faces are hat-labelled; the cut takes those whole shells. Clean = they hold at least minOwnShells of the hat-labelled faces (most of the hat is its own shells, so no surface is cut) and the hat-labelled faces left in shared shells have their cut rim under the hat (inside its horizontal outline grown by rimM, below its top). Not clean: the hat stays welded in the A mesh, rigid on Head. hairRule false: a person's own cap was generated with their own hair and already fits it; the hair-under-hat rule is for a hat moved onto another head (the G path). Applied here it pulled the guard's fringe under the brim into spikes, which the LOD0 reduction opened into dark cracks (2026-10-27).

rest.note: Sky via Aster, 2026-10-27: the rest is the pose the person was generated in (the intake A-pose), not a T-pose: the mesh is never re-posed at rest, so it matches the raw mesh exactly. The Humanoid reference (the reference T-pose with Latch's neutral legs) is not baked into the mesh: it is a separate armature-only FBX (<id>_H_avatarT.fbx) for Unity's avatar (Copy From Other Avatar), and the same zero is stored on the armature (fit_zero) for the Blender retarget.

deliverables.note: What the determinism check compares byte for byte: everything a later stage or Unity reads (basis, fit, a: FBX, JSON, labels, textures). Found and fixed on the way: the FBX tangent space (MikkTSpace binormals differ run to run on these meshes: not exported, Unity recomputes); dict order from Python sets in the stats (keys sorted); wall-clock timings (moved to work/); the FBX header's ApplicationNativeFile and the texture FileName/RelativeFilename/Path (absolute paths: written as bare names, so the same build gives the same bytes in any folder). The .blend files are working files under work/: Blender writes pointer-keyed lists in an order that varies between processes even with a fixed Python hash seed (measured), so they are never a deliverable.

lod0.note: GDD §01 house rule: models ship at full detail, no decimation without Sky's sign-off. LOD0 is the generated mesh as delivered (50k faces, its own normals, valid because the rest is the source pose); LOD1 and LOD2 (4.5k, 1.5k) are decimated from it as today's figures' LOD chain does. The fit test decimated LOD0 to 12k and cleared the normals: that is what made the faces facet.

armpit.note: in the armpit band (upper-arm weight within band, at least torsoMin on Spine1, Spine2 or a shoulder) weights are averaged over every vertex within mergeM in space, so the sleeve shell and the body shell (separate shells in image-to-3D meshes) move as one: an arm raised to horizontal opened a slit between them (e2e_coat) and crumpled the sleeve (e2e_guard).

personNote: person: the intake prompt's person slot, copied from paid/069-intake/ledger.jsonl (heights come from it by fit.json heights)

engineSpeeds.note: Unity-measured planted-foot speeds (Latch's import measure) replace the Blender value for these clips; scaled by the new skeleton's leg length against the measured one
